acceptance_basis: Independent inspection of the new fixed wrapper/schema adapter and entire prior v6c scope; exact hash-checked old assembler reuse; ten fixed input records plus helper; seven prior child bindings; unchanged images/source maps/calls; independently accepted v6d evidence with 43 app source witnesses; accepted diagnostic/guard consumer deltas; independent twelve-draft reconstruction and fifteen synthetic tests. policy_meanings.entrypoint_side_effects: The applicable startup/client effects are characterized and permitted within this profile, not asserted nonexistent. Only four applications are startup targets; the three existing storage daemons remain running.
policy_meanings.no_proxy_redirect: Reviewed fixed-recipient HTTP clients and explicitly listed restricted storage/client commands in this profile; not arbitrary unrestricted image/daemon operations.
policy_meanings.zero_retries: Original fixed-loopback HTTP transport and reviewed restricted application-call retry controls. Not zero physical socket attempts, DNS/address results, all pool assignments or all daemon operations. Distinct planned health/read calls are not retries of each other.

preserved_limits: Acceptance is source/configuration policy proof for the listed hash-bound profile, not observed startup, SDK initialization, endpoint success or a citation result.

HTTPcore pool reassignment and Psycopg address fallback remain disclosed. No blanket absence of duplicate business effects or lower-layer connection attempts is asserted; no duplicate execution was observed by this review.
Only planned client checks against already-running storage are assessed; no storage daemon-wide no-retry, background-effect or effect-free-entrypoint claim is made.

Four app source bindings include accepted preparation-controller attestations; older matching-image SDK captures and new-memory source-only inheritance retain their stated provenance distinctions. The policy accepts the specified bytes, not an unverified future installation.
Existing fresh identity/image/configuration/installed-source/namespace/recipient/lineage/archive/citation gates are not waived, replaced by this packet or declared passed.
No general market/news/model capability is removed or accepted as ready. No current-market causal truth, profitability, trading eligibility or production deployment is inferred.
Records remain meaningful only with this scope, the reviewed consumers and exact subjects/source pins; arbitrary use of the same images is outside acceptance.

Separately accepted dormant-nonrecipient exception: an unselected row on the reviewed network may have a blank reported ID only when created, never started, exact-int zero restarts, restart policy no, no existing reserved recipient alias, and the existing network.project endpoint/address/identity checks pass. Its row remains in the full-inventory ownership scan. This is an intentional eligibility acceptance difference, not policy parity.

Wrong reported IDs, nonempty contradictory endpoint/address evidence, reserved-alias collisions and restart/state drift still refuse. Post-start recipient_checks still requires real attachment and pinned selected identities; configured projection is not connectivity.

Only null/empty IPAM are equivalent. Complete declared final aliases remain MODELLED. No extra daemon alias is stripped or guessed equivalent. Actual activation must pass the existing fresh fail-closed identity/configuration/installed-source/namespace/storage/recipient/lineage/archive/citation gates.

Optional recipient diagnostics are fixed-label, selected-name-only/otherwise-null, sanitized again at receipt. First refusal follows traversal order and is not a unique cause; exceptions can produce broad bounded categories, and later predicates can be unevaluated. No raw exception, unselected name, network payload, environment or token is exported by this diagnostic acceptance.

All three restricted policy meanings remain literal: not zero physical connection/DNS/pool attempts, not effect-free startup, and not arbitrary image/daemon approval. Existing HTTPcore/Psycopg fallback and version-specific private S3 retry-hook limitations remain.
